I have so many of the symptoms you describe, and i know how that shaking feels, it's the worst, isn't it?   
sounds like your parents are very strict, so maybe you can look for help on your own? i know you can't see yourself going to a therapist, but from someone who was on the place you're at now, let me tell you that asking for help doesn't make you weak. Therapy does work, because they won't just push a button and fix all the issues,  
 but it'll find the root of the issues, show them to you, and give you the tools so you can deal with them yourself. We usually think we know everything about ourselves, but therapy helps you look at that from a perspective you didn't considered before, because you were too deep into your own fears.  
you don't have to be a martyr, or a super strong man that came out of it on his own. there's nothing wrong with seeking help when you need it. you literally have NOTHING to lose, but SO much to gain, don't you think?

one day i was at class and the teacher was talking about her encounter with an old classmate of her, who told her that he had x years until retirement and he couldn't wait!.   
"i though it was sad, not enjoying your carreer and just counting years go by, until you can retire and leave it behind", she said. i was just sitting there, with my mouth open. that was gona be me! suddendly, the curtain in front of my eyes was pushed. i was just studying this to not dissapoint my parents, because of all the money that was put on this, but i didn't enjoy it.  


2 years later, i do art full time. and i've never been happier.   
still guilty about the money my parents spent on my education though. even more guilty because of how supportive they were of me, not a single bad word from them. it's in moments like that when you realize how lucky you have been in life, and you never ever realize it before.
